cards.explanation: The answer is forever and ever. David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), says, "I will bless Your name forever and ever." He wears a crown, and he still calls God "…my God and King…" There's no retirement date on that praise, friends.
The answer is False. David says, "Every day I will bless You, and I will praise Your name forever and ever." He doesn't wait for a parade. Every. Single. Day, friends. Ordinary days get praise too.

The answer is generation. David says, "One generation will commend Your works to the next, and will proclaim Your mighty acts…" He's picturing the news getting passed down, one group to the next. It's like a recipe handed down from one cook to the next, except this news is the best thing to pass along.

The answer is True. David writes, "They will proclaim the power of Your awesome deeds, and I will declare Your greatness." He doesn't just sit in the audience while others do the talking. He joins the choir himself, friends.
The answer is False. David says the LORD is "…slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion." He's also gracious and compassionate. Slow to anger, friends. I've got a lot to learn there.
The answer is, to all He has made. David says, "The LORD is good to all; His compassion rests on all He has made." Look how big that circle is, friends. David doesn't draw a smaller one inside it.

The answer is False. David says, "All You have made will give You thanks, O LORD, and Your saints will bless You." The thanks comes from all He has made, and the saints are mentioned too. David's circle keeps getting wider, bakers.

The answer is, so people would know His mighty acts. David says they will speak of the glory of God's kingdom "…to make known to men Your mighty acts and the glorious splendor of Your kingdom." The talking has a job, friends. It's about people getting to know what God has done.
The answer is everlasting. David says, "Your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and Your dominion endures through all generations." Kingdoms usually have an end date, bakers. This one doesn't.

The answer is True. David says, "The LORD is faithful in all His words and kind in all His actions." All His words, not most of them. Most of us keep our word right up until the snooze button gets involved.

The answer is, He holds them up and lifts them. David says, "The LORD upholds all who fall and lifts up all who are bowed down." The word is all, and the LORD does the lifting. I've fallen off the counter plenty, friends, and a hand like that sounds mighty good.

The answer is, their food in season. David says, "The eyes of all look to You, and You give them their food in season." Food in season means the right food at the right time. I wish my cookie orders showed up that well timed, bakers.

The answer is False. David says, "The LORD is righteous in all His ways and kind in all His deeds." He doesn't add a test to pass first, friends. Earlier he even says, "The LORD is good to all…" (Psalm 145:9).

The answer is, those who call on Him in truth. David says, "The LORD is near to all who call on Him, to all who call out to Him in truth." It's about calling out to Him, and doing it in truth. You don't need a fancy title or a special building, friends.

The answer is, He hears them and saves them. David says, "He fulfills the desires of those who fear Him; He hears their cry and saves them." The LORD hears and the LORD saves. I know a little about crying out from the back of a dark junk drawer where I sat for years, and this verse hits home, bakers.

The answer is False. David says, "The LORD preserves all who love Him, but all the wicked He will destroy." The two groups are not treated the same. It's a heavy line, friends, and it's good to take it seriously.

The answer is creature. David ends with, "let every creature bless His holy name forever and ever." Every creature, friends, not just the ones with a speaking part. And look at those last words. They're the same ones he started with.
